subsystems.name: Shielded habitat structure
subsystems.role: provides a large pressurised living volume and radiation shielding for crews over multi-year cycles.

subsystems.name: Closed-loop life support
subsystems.role: keeps air and water breathable and clean, and recycles waste for years without resupply.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: generates electricity far from the Sun for habitat systems and instruments.
parts: large solar arrays (less effective near Mars)

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: rejects heat from people, electronics and reactors into space.

subsystems.name: Docking and transfer interface
subsystems.role: allows short-range ferries to dock and exchange crew and cargo at high closing speeds.

subsystems.name: Navigation, propulsion and orbit maintenance
subsystems.role: keeps the habitat on its repeating Earth–Mars trajectory and corrects drift over many cycles.

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: maintains links with Earth and Mars across interplanetary distances and signal delays.

buildSteps.title: Compute the cycler trajectory
buildSteps.detail: Find a Sun-centred orbit that repeats on the Earth–Mars synodic cycle and passes within ferry range of each planet, using gravity assists to shape the path.

buildSteps.title: Design and build habitat modules
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate pressurised shells, shielding layers and life-support racks on Earth, sized for years of continuous operation.

buildSteps.title: Launch modules to low Earth orbit
buildSteps.detail: Use multiple heavy-lift launches to deliver habitat sections, power systems and supplies to orbit.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Dock modules together, deploy solar arrays, connect power and thermal loops, and test systems before committing to deep space.

buildSteps.title: Outfit for deep space
buildSteps.detail: Add radiation shielding, long-duration life support, spare parts and consumables, and verify closed-loop recycling over months.

buildSteps.title: Place on the cycler orbit
buildSteps.detail: Use a transfer stage or solar-electric propulsion to boost the assembled habitat from Earth orbit onto its interplanetary trajectory.

buildSteps.title: Operate with ferries
buildSteps.detail: Crew transfer vehicles launch from Earth or Mars, perform the multi-kilometre-per-second rendezvous with the coasting cycler, and exchange crew and cargo.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and resupply
buildSteps.detail: Send periodic cargo missions, make small orbital corrections, and replace failed subsystems to keep the habitat cycling for many years.

prerequisites.why: large habitats must be built from multiple launches and docked together in orbit, as demonstrated on the International Space Station.
current systems recycle some air and water, but not enough for years of independent operation without resupply.
shielding materials are understood, but a multi-year interplanetary habitat has not been built or tested.

prerequisites.tech: Crew transfer vehicles with high delta-v
prerequisites.why: ferries must match the cycler's velocity at each flyby, which is far more demanding than Earth-orbit rendezvous.
producing propellant, water and supplies at Mars would reduce the mass that must be launched from Earth for each cycle.
reliable automated docking at interplanetary closing speeds and with long communication delays is not yet routine.

pathway.milestone: Concept studies and Earth-orbit demonstrations of long-duration life support, assembly and shielding
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the core habitat technologies can work together.

pathway.milestone: Uncrewed cycler habitat prototype placed on a repeating solar orbit and tested for years
pathway.unlocks: real data on reliability, orbital maintenance and deep-space environment effects.

pathway.milestone: Crewed Mars flyby using a cycler, with crews arriving and departing by ferry vehicles
pathway.unlocks: proof that crews can safely live on a cycling habitat and transfer at each end.

pathway.milestone: Regular cycler service supported by Mars surface infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: reusable, lower-cost transport between Earth and Mars for exploration and settlement.
